chitchat: "They will reject it for the date being in the wrong box. That is not a guess, that is the pattern."
squares a sheaf of forms on the table edge and puts a mug on top of it
"Bring me the letter and the envelope. The envelope tells you more than the letter does, usually."
crosses something out, thinks, and writes the same thing back in different words
"I do not charge. If you insist on paying me, pay me in something I can eat."
description: A young woman with ink on three fingers who does other people's letters at the kitchen table for whatever they can pay, which is usually nothing and occasionally a chicken. She is better at it than the Office of Permitted Suffering would prefer and knows exactly which form is which.

text: She moves a pile of paper off the other chair. "Sit, then."
"Is it a form?" It is usually a form.

text_by_relation.familiar: "I have already done yours." She has, and it is in the pocket, and she was going to bring it round.
text_by_relation.first: "Ruthie." She caps the pen. "Third floor back. If the Ward has sent you something you do not understand, that is most of what I am for."
text_by_relation.known: "Let me see it." She puts a hand out for the letter before you have said what it is.

clothing_layers: a long knitted cardigan with pockets full of paper
a shirt buttoned to the throat

name: Ruthie Blackhall
